sections.figure_alt: A forward block and a return path that is subtracted at the input.
sections.body_md:
The loop transfer function \(L(s)\) is the product of every block you meet walking once around the loop. Start at the error, go through the forward path to the output, then through the return path back to the summing junction. That product tells you the loop gain at each frequency and determines stability and performance.

The closed-loop transfer function \(T(s) = G/(1+GH)\) is what the reference sees. The sensitivity \(S(s) = 1/(1+L)\) is what a disturbance sees. Together \(T + S = 1\). The return difference \(1 + L\) is what converts open-loop behavior to closed-loop behavior.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
Loop gain: \(L(s) = G(s) H(s)\).

Closed-loop (complementary sensitivity): \(T(s) = \dfrac{G(s)}{1 + G(s)H(s)} = \dfrac{L(s)}{1 + L(s)}\).

Sensitivity: \(S(s) = \dfrac{1}{1 + L(s)}\).

Constraint: \(T(s) + S(s) = 1\). A disturbance at the output is multiplied by \(S\), so larger \(L\) means smaller disturbance effect.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: Take \(G = 10\) and \(H = 0.2\). The loop gain is \(L = 10 \times 0.2 = 2\). The closed-loop gain is \(T = 10/3 = 3.333\). The sensitivity is \(S = 1/3 = 0.333\). Check: \(T + S = 3.333 + 0.333 \approx 1\) after rounding. A unit disturbance at the output is reduced to 0.333. Using the loop gain 2 as the closed-loop gain is wrong; 2 is the product around the loop, not the gain from reference to output.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: The loop gain is not the closed-loop gain. The loop gain is the open-loop product around the loop. The closed-loop gain divides by \(1 + L\). Confusing sensitivity with complementary sensitivity swaps what the reference sees and what the disturbance sees. The return difference \(1 + L\) is not the loop gain; it is one more than the loop gain. On a Nyquist plot, the critical point is \(-1\), not \(0\) or \(1\).

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: A Nyquist plot draws \(L(j\omega)\) in the complex plane and counts encirclements of \(-1\) to determine stability. Sensitivity analysis asks how large \(S(j\omega)\) can be before the loop is too sensitive to disturbances. Robust performance bounds combine \(S\) and \(T\) with uncertainty descriptions. The loop transfer function is the central object in all of these analyses.
